spec.name: SMV time-study ingestion schema
spec.purpose: Define the record shape a factory (or a synthetic generator) must produce so that calibration_fit.py can refit the taxonomy's calibration-pending coefficients. Each record is one *continuously-timed observation* of a single engine element, seam segment, or full operation, captured by direct time study (stopwatch / MOST-style video analysis) or a work-sampling system.
design_principles: One row = one timed instance of one element/seam/operation occurrence, never a pre-averaged value -- averaging belongs in the fitting step, not the ingestion step, so residual variance is preserved for the diagnostics report.

Every row carries the exact parameter values the engine itself needs to recompute its predicted time for that instance (echoing compute_element's/assemble_operation's own **params kwargs) -- calibration is a regression of observed_s against the engine's own predictors, not against a separate hand-built feature set.

The schema is hierarchical to match the taxonomy's own hierarchy of calibration-pending scope: engine-level constants (a_steer, b_arm, ...) are shared across all factories; factory-level parameters (PHI reference fabric B_ref/MIU_ref/t_ref_mm, pace v_guide) are shared across operators within one factory; operator-level (Gamma_skill) varies per person. A study batch declares which scope it can identify.

Provenance and rater/method metadata travel with every row so the diagnostics report can flag studies with too few reps, non-standard-performance raters, or fabric/machine combinations outside the taxonomy's reference set.
Nothing is silently dropped: rows failing schema validation are rejected with a reason, not coerced.

conventions.time_units: seconds, continuous (not TMU) -- convert to TMU only for reporting, never for fitting
conventions.identifiers: element codes and machine/attachment codes MUST match element_taxonomy.json / machine_classes.csv exactly; the loader validates against those files at ingestion time and rejects unknown codes
conventions.missing_values: use JSON null, never a sentinel number (-1, 999, etc.)
conventions.one_file_per_batch: a 'study_batch' groups all rows collected under one method/rater/date-range; batches are the unit of provenance and inter-rater comparison

study_batch.description: Top-level container. One JSON file (or one row-group in a long-format CSV/Parquet loader) is one study_batch.

fields.name: factory_id
fields.description: Which factory/site this batch was collected at. Determines factory-level scope (PHI reference fabric, pace).

fields.name: method
fields.description: Time-study method. SYNTHETIC marks generator-produced rows (e.g. this project's own diagnostics demo) so they can be excluded from any real-data fit.

fields.name: rater_id
fields.description: Analyst or system that performed the timing/pace-rating.

fields.name: rater_qualification
fields.description: Used to weight or flag batches in diagnostics; automated/video-derived batches typically have zero pace-rating subjectivity but may have segmentation error instead.

fields.name: performance_rating_applied
fields.description: Whether observed_s values in this batch have already been normalized to standard pace (rating factor applied) by the collector. If false, calibration_fit.py applies pace_rating_pct itself per row.

observation.description: One timed instance. Exactly one of element_observation / seam_observation / cycle_observation / operation_observation must be present, matching the scope of what was timed.

fields.name: operator_id
fields.description: Pseudonymous operator identifier. Required even for element-level rows so Gamma_skill can eventually be fit per operator; use a shared placeholder (e.g. 'UNSPECIFIED') only for batches that cannot identify the operator.

fields.name: pace_rating_pct
fields.description: Analyst's pace rating (100 = standard performance) for this specific instance, if performance_rating_applied is false at the batch level and rating was done per-observation rather than per-batch.

fields.name: n_reps_averaged
fields.description: Must be 1 for a single continuously-timed instance (the design principle above). Values >1 are accepted for legacy pre-averaged data but are down-weighted in fitting and flagged in diagnostics.

fields.name: observed_s
fields.description: The measured elapsed time in seconds for exactly the scope named below (one element occurrence / one seam pass / one cycle / one full operation) -- standard-performance-normalized if performance_rating_applied.

fields.name: element_observation
fields.description: Present when this row times a single handling element occurrence.

element_code.description: Must match a code in element_taxonomy.json elements[].code (e.g. 'HAM', 'HGD').

params.description: The exact **params that would be passed to Taxonomy.compute_element(element_code, **params) to predict this instance -- e.g. {'distance_cm': 25.0, 'plies': 2, 'match_precision': 'P2', 'fabric_class': 'REF_POPLIN'}. Any parameter accepted by the element's signature and not supplied falls back to the taxonomy default, exactly as compute_element does; the loader records which fields were defaulted for the diagnostics report, since defaulted fields cannot be used to identify parameter sensitivity from this row.

fields.name: seam_observation
fields.description: Present when this row times one pass along a stitched seam (a t_guide- or t_machine-dominated instance).

binding_side_hint.description: Optional analyst judgment of which pillar was visibly binding; used only as a diagnostics cross-check against the engine's own MAX() selection, never fed into the fit directly.

fields.name: cycle_observation
fields.description: Present when this row times one cycle-machine program run (buttonhole/bartack/button-sew).

fields.name: operation_observation
fields.description: Present when this row times a full multi-step operation end-to-end (coarsest grain; informs BT_op/ST_op-level reconciliation and Gamma_skill, not individual coefficients).

engine_step_sequence.description: The same steps= list shape smv_assembly.Operation takes, so the loader can compute the engine's predicted BT_op_s for direct comparison to observed_s.

fabric_class_actual.description: If different from the reference fabric assumed in params/fabric_class, e.g. the factory's own denim vs. REF_POPLIN -- flags a fabric-difficulty PHI extrapolation.

calibration_scope_map.description: Which observation kind identifies which calibration-pending symbol/element, used by calibration_fit.py to route rows to the right regression and by the coverage report to flag symbols with zero supporting observations.

routes.notes: The primary route for identifying per-phase-type coefficients; distinct element_code + varied params (esp. distance/plies/mass) needed to separate intercept from slope terms.

Also cross-checked against machine_time.py's pure_machine_time_seam so a seam row can attribute variance to the guide pillar specifically when binding_side_hint == 'guide' or the engine's own MAX() selects guide.
Currently used for machine_time.py's cycle-time model validation, not for taxonomy coefficient fitting -- cycle machines run a taught program, not an operator steering law.

Coarse-grained; used to fit operator-level Gamma_skill (given already-fit engine constants) and to detect factory-level PHI reference-fabric mis-specification from aggregate residuals when element-level data is too sparse.

on_ingest: element_code / machine_class / attachment codes exist in element_taxonomy.json / machine_classes.csv
params keys are a subset of the element's declared parameter names (mirrors handling_time.Taxonomy._resolve_params's unknown-parameter check)
params values respect each parameter's declared domain (mirrors the domain-bound check added to _resolve_params)
pace_rating_pct, if present, lies in [50, 150]; rows outside this range are rejected, not clipped
on_fit: n_reps_averaged == 1 rows are weighted 1.0; n_reps_averaged > 1 rows are weighted 1/n_reps_averaged (a pre-averaged observation contributes to the mean but not to residual-variance estimation the way a raw rep would)
SYNTHETIC-method batches are excluded from any fit against real coefficients by default; calibration_fit.py requires an explicit include_synthetic=True to mix them in
a coefficient is only reported as fit (not left at its taxonomy default) once its minimum-observation-count threshold is met -- see calibration_fit.py MIN_OBS_PER_COEFFICIENT
